entities.blurb: Stained terracotta is a dyed variant of terracotta obtained by crafting undyed terracotta with dyes. Some of the variants are found in badlands biomes, and all variants can be smelted into glazed terracotta.
entities.name: Lime Terracotta

entities.blurb: A banner is a block that can be crafted in 16 different colors, customized in a loom using dyes and banner patterns, and applied to a shield. In Java Edition, banners can also be used to add markers to maps.
entities.name: Lime Wall Banner

entities.blurb: Wool is a block obtained from sheep that can be dyed in any of the sixteen different colors. It can be used as a crafting material and to block vibrations.
entities.name: Lime Wool

entities.blurb: A wool slab is a craftable slab variant of wool. It can be dyed in all 16 colors.
entities.name: Lime Wool Slab

entities.blurb: Wool stairs are a craftable stair variant of wool. They can be dyed in all 16 colors.
entities.name: Lime Wool Stairs

entities.blurb: A lodestone is a block that can be used to alter compasses to point toward it.
entities.name: Lodestone

entities.blurb: A loom is a block used to apply customizable and layerable designs to banners using dyes. Some designs require banner patterns to apply. It also serves as a shepherd's job site block.
entities.name: Loom

entities.blurb: A banner is a block that can be crafted in 16 different colors, customized in a loom using dyes and banner patterns, and applied to a shield. In Java Edition, banners can also be used to add markers to maps.
entities.name: Magenta Banner

entities.blurb: A bed is a dyeable utility block that allows a player in the Overworld to sleep through the night and change their spawn point to within a few blocks of the bed, as long as it is not broken or obstructed. Villagers sleep in beds at night and require spare beds to produce offspring.
entities.name: Magenta Bed

entities.blurb:
A candle is a dyable block that emits light when lit with a flint and steel. Up to four of the same color of candle can be placed in one block space, which affects the amount of light produced.
Dyed candles are the dyed variants of candles that come in all sixteen colors. Once dyed, they cannot be changed into a different color.
entities.name: Magenta Candle

entities.blurb:
A cake is a block that can serve as food. It can be eaten by placing and using it, with each use consuming one of its seven slices. The entire cake gives the most hunger points out of every food item, but has low saturation.
A cake with candle is an uneaten cake with any type of candle placed on it, which can be lit with a flint and steel to emit light.
entities.name: Cake with Magenta Candle

entities.blurb: Carpets are thin variants of wool that can be dyed in any of the 16 colors.
entities.name: Magenta Carpet

entities.blurb: Concrete is a block created when concrete powder touches water. It comes in the sixteen dye colors.
entities.name: Magenta Concrete

entities.blurb: Concrete powder is a gravity-affected block that is converted to concrete when touching water. It comes in the sixteen dye colors.
entities.name: Magenta Concrete Powder

entities.blurb: Concrete slabs are a craftable slab variant of concrete. They come in 16 colors.
entities.name: Magenta Concrete Slab

entities.blurb: Concrete stairs are a craftable stair variant of concrete. They come in 16 colors.
entities.name: Magenta Concrete Stairs

entities.blurb: Glazed terracotta is a vibrant solid block that comes in the sixteen regular dye colors, obtained by smelting stained terracotta. Glazed terracotta does not stick to slime blocks or honey blocks, and it cannot be pulled by sticky pistons, but it can be pushed by pistons.
entities.name: Magenta Glazed Terracotta

entities.blurb: A shulker box is a dyeable block that stores items, and, unlike all other storage blocks, keeps its contents in item form when broken.
entities.name: Magenta Shulker Box

entities.blurb: Stained glass is a dyed variant of the glass block.
entities.name: Magenta Stained Glass

entities.blurb: A stained glass pane is a dyed version of a glass pane. It is a transparent block that can be used as a more efficient alternative to stained glass blocks.
entities.name: Magenta Stained Glass Pane

entities.blurb: Stained terracotta is a dyed variant of terracotta obtained by crafting undyed terracotta with dyes. Some of the variants are found in badlands biomes, and all variants can be smelted into glazed terracotta.
entities.name: Magenta Terracotta

entities.blurb: A banner is a block that can be crafted in 16 different colors, customized in a loom using dyes and banner patterns, and applied to a shield. In Java Edition, banners can also be used to add markers to maps.
entities.name: Magenta Wall Banner

entities.blurb: Wool is a block obtained from sheep that can be dyed in any of the sixteen different colors. It can be used as a crafting material and to block vibrations.
entities.name: Magenta Wool

entities.blurb: A wool slab is a craftable slab variant of wool. It can be dyed in all 16 colors.
entities.name: Magenta Wool Slab

entities.blurb: Wool stairs are a craftable stair variant of wool. They can be dyed in all 16 colors.
entities.name: Magenta Wool Stairs

entities.blurb: A magma block is a light-emitting block found underwater in the Overworld, and commonly in the Nether. It deals burning damage while stood on, which can be prevented by sneaking. Underwater magma blocks produce bubble columns that pull entities downward and provide air.
entities.name: Magma Block

entities.blurb: A wooden button is a type of button that remains pressed for longer than a stone button and can additionally be pressed by arrows and thrown tridents.
entities.name: Mangrove Button

entities.blurb: The wooden door is a variant of the door made of wood that can be opened and closed by the player without redstone.
entities.name: Mangrove Door

entities.blurb: A wooden fence is the wooden variant of fences, crafted using planks and sticks.
entities.name: Mangrove Fence

entities.blurb: A fence gate is a block that shares the functions of both the door and the fence.
entities.name: Mangrove Fence Gate

entities.blurb: A hanging sign is a variant of a  sign that displays text, and can be placed underneath blocks or with a solid self-supporting bracket. The text of hanging signs can be customized with dyes and glow ink sacs, and they can be waxed to prevent edits.
entities.name: Mangrove Hanging Sign

entities.blurb: Leaves are transparent blocks that generate as part of trees and are sources of their respective saplings. They dissipate over time when not attached to logs, but persist when placed by players. Falling-leaf particles occasionally drop from leaves.
entities.name: Mangrove Leaves

entities.blurb: A log or stem is a naturally occurring block found in trees or huge fungi, primarily used as a building block and to create planks, a versatile crafting ingredient. There are currently ten types of logs: oak, spruce, birch, jungle, acacia, dark oak, mangrove, cherry, pale oak and poplar; and two types of stems: crimson and warped.
entities.name: Mangrove Log

entities.blurb: Planks are common blocks used as building blocks and in crafting recipes. They are usually one of the first things that a player crafts in Survival mode. There are currently 13 variants of planks, which can be differentiated into three categories: Overworld planks made from tree logs, bamboo planks made from blocks of bamboo, and nonflammable Nether planks made from huge fungus stems.
entities.name: Mangrove Planks

entities.blurb: A wooden pressure plate is a wooden variant of the pressure plate. It can detect all entities, producing the maximum signal strength of 15. Wooden pressure plates come in all variants of wood.
entities.name: Mangrove Pressure Plate

entities.blurb: A mangrove propagule is an amphibious sapling that can grow into a mangrove tree. They grow hanging from mangrove leaves when the leaves are bone mealed or when a tree is first created, but can only be obtained as items if fully grown.
entities.name: Mangrove Propagule

entities.blurb: Mangrove roots are blocks that form as part of mangrove trees. Unlike other see-through blocks such as copper grates, mangrove roots are capable of conducting redstone power.
entities.name: Mangrove Roots

entities.blurb:
A shelf is a block that can store and display up to three stacks of items. Using an item slot exchanges its contents with the player's hotbar. Powering a shelf combines its three slots together and makes using it swap everything at once.
Two or three adjacent shelves can merge their slots together if all are powered, which allows for swapping six or nine items at a time, respectively.
entities.name: Mangrove Shelf

entities.blurb: A sign is a non-solid block that can display text, and can be placed on the top or side of other blocks. The text of signs can be customized with dyes and glow ink sacs, and they can be waxed to prevent its text from being edited by any player.
entities.name: Mangrove Sign

entities.blurb: A wooden slab is a wooden variant of a slab crafted from its respective planks.
entities.name: Mangrove Slab

entities.blurb: Wooden stairs are a wooden variant of stairs, crafted from their respective planks.
entities.name: Mangrove Stairs

entities.blurb: A wooden trapdoor is a variant of the trapdoor that can be opened and closed by the player without redstone.
entities.name: Mangrove Trapdoor

entities.blurb: A hanging sign is a variant of a  sign that displays text, and can be placed underneath blocks or with a solid self-supporting bracket. The text of hanging signs can be customized with dyes and glow ink sacs, and they can be waxed to prevent edits.
entities.name: Mangrove Wall Hanging Sign

entities.blurb: A sign is a non-solid block that can display text, and can be placed on the top or side of other blocks. The text of signs can be customized with dyes and glow ink sacs, and they can be waxed to prevent its text from being edited by any player.
entities.name: Mangrove Wall Sign

entities.blurb: Wood or hyphae is a block that has the log's "bark" texture on all six sides. It comes in 12 types: oak, spruce, birch, jungle, acacia, dark oak, mangrove, cherry, crimson, warped, pale oak, and poplar.
entities.name: Mangrove Wood

entities.blurb:
Amethyst buds are the first three stages of growth of amethyst clusters, which grow on budding amethyst.
Amethyst clusters are the fourth and final growth stage of amethyst buds, which drop amethyst shards when mined.
entities.name: Medium Amethyst Bud

entities.blurb: A melon is a fruit block that grows from a fully-grown melon stem, which in turn is grown from melon seeds.
entities.name: Melon

entities.blurb:
Melon seeds are items obtained from melon slices that can be used to grow melon stems.
Melon stems are plants grown on farmland that, over time, grow melons on dirt, mud and moss blocks adjacent to them.
entities.name: Melon Stem

entities.blurb: A moss block is a natural block that can be spread to other blocks by using bone meal.
entities.name: Moss Block

entities.blurb: A moss carpet is a thin decorative variant of the moss block, resembling a carpet in functionality.
entities.name: Moss Carpet

entities.blurb: Mossy cobblestone is a variant of cobblestone with moss on it. It is mainly used for crafting or as a building block.
entities.name: Mossy Cobblestone

entities.blurb: A mossy cobblestone slab is a decorative slab variant of mossy cobblestone that generates in pillager outposts and is used for building.
entities.name: Mossy Cobblestone Slab

entities.blurb: Mossy cobblestone stairs are a decorative stairs variant of mossy cobblestone that generate in pillager outposts and are used for building.
entities.name: Mossy Cobblestone Stairs

entities.blurb: A mossy cobblestone wall is a decorative wall variant of mossy cobblestone that generates as part of pillager outposts and is used for building.
entities.name: Mossy Cobblestone Wall

entities.blurb: A mossy stone brick slab is a decorative slab variant of mossy stone bricks that generates in ruined portals and is used for building.
entities.name: Mossy Stone Brick Slab

entities.blurb: Mossy stone brick stairs are a stairs variant of mossy stone bricks that generate in ruined portals and are used for building.
entities.name: Mossy Stone Brick Stairs

entities.blurb: A mossy stone brick wall is a decorative wall variant of mossy stone bricks that generates in ruined portals and is used for building.
entities.name: Mossy Stone Brick Wall

entities.blurb: Mossy stone bricks are a variant of stone bricks.
entities.name: Mossy Stone Bricks

entities.blurb: Pistons and sticky pistons have 2 technical blocks that cannot be obtained. These include the piston head and moving piston blocks.
entities.name: Moving Piston

entities.blurb: Mud is a block found abundantly in mangrove swamps or created by using a water bottle on any type of dirt block. It can be used for crafting or converted into clay using pointed dripstone.
entities.name: Mud

entities.blurb: A mud brick slab is a decorative slab variant of mud bricks that generates in trail ruins and is used for building.
entities.name: Mud Brick Slab

entities.blurb: Mud brick stairs are a decorative stairs variant of mud bricks that generate in trail ruins and are used for building.
entities.name: Mud Brick Stairs

entities.blurb: A mud brick wall is a decorative wall variant of mud bricks that generates in trail ruins and is used for building.
entities.name: Mud Brick Wall

entities.blurb: Mud bricks are a block obtained by crafting 4 packed mud.
entities.name: Mud Bricks

entities.blurb: Muddy mangrove roots are a decorative variant of mangrove roots with dirt-like properties.
entities.name: Muddy Mangrove Roots

entities.blurb: A mushroom block is a solid block that makes up a huge mushroom, which consists of a mushroom stem and brown mushroom blocks or red mushroom blocks, depending on the color of the huge mushroom.
entities.name: Mushroom Stem

entities.blurb: Mycelium is a particularly rare variant of dirt that is only found naturally in mushroom fields biomes. It has a particle effect that resembles tiny spores being released constantly from the surface.
entities.name: Mycelium

entities.blurb: A Nether brick fence is a Nether brick variant of fences used to form Nether fortresses in the Nether.
entities.name: Nether Brick Fence

entities.blurb: A Nether brick slab is a decorative slab variant of Nether bricks that does not generate naturally and is used for building.
entities.name: Nether Brick Slab

entities.blurb: Nether brick stairs are a decorative stairs variant of Nether bricks that generate in Nether fortress staircases and are used for building.
entities.name: Nether Brick Stairs

entities.blurb: A Nether brick wall is a decorative wall variant of Nether bricks that does not generate naturally and is used for building.
entities.name: Nether Brick Wall

entities.blurb: Nether bricks are the building blocks of Nether fortresses in the Nether and are used to spawn mobs in that structure.
entities.name: Nether Bricks

entities.blurb: Nether gold ore is a type of gold ore found in the Nether that drops gold nuggets instead of raw gold when broken. As with other gold blocks, breaking Nether gold ore will anger nearby piglins.
entities.name: Nether Gold Ore

entities.blurb: The Nether portal block is the translucent part of the Nether portal that teleports the player to and from the Nether.
entities.name: Nether Portal

entities.blurb: Nether quartz ore is an ore found in the Nether, and is a source of quartz.
entities.name: Nether Quartz Ore

entities.blurb: Nether sprouts are a non-solid fungi block that generate in warped forests. Unlike other warped forest plants, it does not have a crimson equivalent.
entities.name: Nether Sprouts

entities.blurb:
Nether wart is a fungus harvested from Nether wart crops and is used to plant them. It is an essential ingredient in almost every potion. Unlike other crimson plants, Nether wart doesn't have a warped equivalent, although warped wart blocks exist.
Nether wart crops are found in Nether fortresses and bastion remnants and used to grow Nether wart, which only requires soul sand to grow.
entities.name: Nether Wart

entities.blurb: Nether wart blocks are decorative blocks found in crimson forests and crafted using Nether wart.
entities.name: Nether Wart Block

entities.blurb: A block of netherite, internally known as a netherite block, is a precious metal block made from nine netherite ingots. In item form, it is immune to fire and lava, but can still be destroyed by a cactus.
entities.name: Block of Netherite

entities.blurb: Netherrack is a frail stone block found abundantly in the Nether. Fire lit on top of netherrack burns indefinitely and cannot be extinguished by rain.
entities.name: Netherrack

entities.blurb: A note block is a block that emits sounds when attacked, used, or powered. The sound produced can be altered in various ways by using it or putting certain blocks directly above or below it. entities.name: Obsidian

entities.name: Orange Tulip

entities.name: Orange Wool Slab

entities.blurb: Wool stairs are a craftable stair variant of wool. They can be dyed in all 16 colors.
entities.name: Orange Wool Stairs

entities.blurb: An oxeye daisy is a flower that can be crafted into light gray dye, suspicious stew, and flower charge banner patterns.
entities.name: Oxeye Daisy

entities.blurb: Chiseled copper is a variant of copper blocks that generates in trial chambers.
entities.name: Oxidized Chiseled Copper

entities.blurb: A block of copper, internally known as a copper block, is a block that oxidizes over time, gaining a verdigris appearance over four stages. They can be prevented from oxidizing by being waxed with honeycombs. Non-oxidized blocks of copper are storage blocks equivalent to nine copper ingots.
entities.name: Oxidized Copper

entities.blurb: Copper bars are copper variants of bars. Unlike iron bars, they are colored copper orange and can oxidize over time, similar to other copper blocks.
entities.name: Oxidized Copper Bars

entities.blurb:
A copper bulb is a light-emitting block. It toggles on or off when it receives a redstone pulse, and does not need continuous power to emit light. Its light level depends on its state of oxidation.
Waxed copper bulbs do not oxidize, but otherwise function identically.
entities.name: Oxidized Copper Bulb

entities.blurb: A copper chain is an oxidizing directional block and the copper variant of chains.
entities.name: Oxidized Copper Chain

entities.blurb:
A copper chest is a type of chest made of copper. It functions almost identically to a normal wooden chest, except that it oxidizes over time, and copper golems remove items from it to store inside nearby wooden chests.
Like normal chests, two copper chests can merge into a large copper chest if placed adjacent each other.
entities.name: Oxidized Copper Chest

entities.blurb: The copper door is a type of door made of copper that can be opened and closed by the player without redstone.
entities.name: Oxidized Copper Door

entities.blurb: A copper golem statue is the result of a copper golem fully oxidizing and petrifying into a block. It can be posed in four different ways, or it can be reanimated by scraping it with an axe enough times.
entities.name: Oxidized Copper Golem Statue

entities.blurb: Copper grates are a variant of copper blocks that have perforations that can be seen through.
entities.name: Oxidized Copper Grate

entities.blurb: A copper lantern is a copper variant of a lantern that displays a green flame and oxidizes over time.
entities.name: Oxidized Copper Lantern

entities.blurb: A copper trapdoor is a type of trapdoor made from copper that can be opened and closed by the player without redstone. A copper trapdoor can exist in one of eight variants depending on how oxidized it is and whether it is waxed or not.
entities.name: Oxidized Copper Trapdoor

entities.blurb: Cut copper is an oxidizing metal block crafted from blocks of copper. Like other copper blocks, cut copper can be waxed to prevent oxidation.
entities.name: Oxidized Cut Copper

entities.blurb: A cut copper slab is a decorative slab variant of cut copper that generates in trial chambers and is used for building. Unlike other types of slabs, cut copper slabs can oxidize over time.
entities.name: Oxidized Cut Copper Slab

entities.blurb: Cut copper stairs are a decorative stairs variant of cut copper that generate in trial chambers and are used for building. Unlike other types of stairs, cut copper stairs can oxidize over time.
entities.name: Oxidized Cut Copper Stairs

entities.blurb: A lightning rod is a block that, with sky access, causes natural lightning strikes in a large area to only target itself. Getting struck by lightning causes it to emit a redstone signal and, if it is not waxed, also reduces its level of oxidation.
entities.name: Oxidized Lightning Rod

entities.blurb: Packed ice is a variant of ice that functions almost identically, but does not melt and is opaque instead of transparent. Like other types of ice, it can only be obtained using a Silk Touch tool.
entities.name: Packed Ice

entities.blurb: Packed mud is a block crafted from mud and wheat. It is used to create mud bricks.
entities.name: Packed Mud

entities.blurb: Pale hanging moss is a block found under the logs and leaves of pale oaks. When attached to a pale oak log or leaves, it emits ambient sounds.
entities.name: Pale Hanging Moss

entities.blurb: A pale moss block is a block that generates in pale gardens. Unlike regular moss blocks, pale moss blocks are flammable.
entities.name: Pale Moss Block

entities.blurb: A pale moss carpet is a block that causes vine-like pale moss to grow on the side of neighboring blocks.
entities.name: Pale Moss Carpet

entities.blurb: A wooden button is a type of button that remains pressed for longer than a stone button and can additionally be pressed by arrows and thrown tridents.
entities.name: Pale Oak Button

entities.blurb: The wooden door is a variant of the door made of wood that can be opened and closed by the player without redstone.
entities.name: Pale Oak Door

entities.blurb: A wooden fence is the wooden variant of fences, crafted using planks and sticks.
entities.name: Pale Oak Fence

entities.blurb: A fence gate is a block that shares the functions of both the door and the fence.
entities.name: Pale Oak Fence Gate

entities.blurb: A hanging sign is a variant of a  sign that displays text, and can be placed underneath blocks or with a solid self-supporting bracket. The text of hanging signs can be customized with dyes and glow ink sacs, and they can be waxed to prevent edits.
entities.name: Pale Oak Hanging Sign

entities.blurb: Leaves are transparent blocks that generate as part of trees and are sources of their respective saplings. They dissipate over time when not attached to logs, but persist when placed by players. Falling-leaf particles occasionally drop from leaves.
entities.name: Pale Oak Leaves

entities.blurb: A log or stem is a naturally occurring block found in trees or huge fungi, primarily used as a building block and to create planks, a versatile crafting ingredient. There are currently ten types of logs: oak, spruce, birch, jungle, acacia, dark oak, mangrove, cherry, pale oak and poplar; and two types of stems: crimson and warped.
entities.name: Pale Oak Log

entities.blurb: Planks are common blocks used as building blocks and in crafting recipes. They are usually one of the first things that a player crafts in Survival mode. There are currently 13 variants of planks, which can be differentiated into three categories: Overworld planks made from tree logs, bamboo planks made from blocks of bamboo, and nonflammable Nether planks made from huge fungus stems.
entities.name: Pale Oak Planks

entities.blurb: A wooden pressure plate is a wooden variant of the pressure plate. It can detect all entities, producing the maximum signal strength of 15. Wooden pressure plates come in all variants of wood.
entities.name: Pale Oak Pressure Plate

entities.blurb: A sapling is a non-solid block that can be grown into a tree.
entities.name: Pale Oak Sapling

entities.blurb:
A shelf is a block that can store and display up to three stacks of items. Using an item slot exchanges its contents with the player's hotbar. Powering a shelf combines its three slots together and makes using it swap everything at once.
Two or three adjacent shelves can merge their slots together if all are powered, which allows for swapping six or nine items at a time, respectively.
entities.name: Pale Oak Shelf

entities.blurb: A sign is a non-solid block that can display text, and can be placed on the top or side of other blocks. The text of signs can be customized with dyes and glow ink sacs, and they can be waxed to prevent its text from being edited by any player.
entities.name: Pale Oak Sign

entities.blurb: A wooden slab is a wooden variant of a slab crafted from its respective planks.
entities.name: Pale Oak Slab

entities.blurb: Wooden stairs are a wooden variant of stairs, crafted from their respective planks.
entities.name: Pale Oak Stairs

entities.blurb: A wooden trapdoor is a variant of the trapdoor that can be opened and closed by the player without redstone.
entities.name: Pale Oak Trapdoor

entities.blurb: A hanging sign is a variant of a  sign that displays text, and can be placed underneath blocks or with a solid self-supporting bracket. The text of hanging signs can be customized with dyes and glow ink sacs, and they can be waxed to prevent edits.
entities.name: Pale Oak Wall Hanging Sign

entities.blurb: A sign is a non-solid block that can display text, and can be placed on the top or side of other blocks. The text of signs can be customized with dyes and glow ink sacs, and they can be waxed to prevent its text from being edited by any player.
entities.name: Pale Oak Wall Sign

entities.blurb: Wood or hyphae is a block that has the log's "bark" texture on all six sides. It comes in 12 types: oak, spruce, birch, jungle, acacia, dark oak, mangrove, cherry, crimson, warped, pale oak, and poplar.
entities.name: Pale Oak Wood

entities.blurb: A froglight is a light-emitting block that is obtained when a frog eats a tiny magma cube. It comes in three variants based on the variant of frog that eats the magma cube.
entities.name: Pearlescent Froglight

entities.blurb: A peony is a tall flower that can be crafted into pink dye.
entities.name: Peony

entities.blurb: A petrified oak slab, known generically as a wooden slab in Bedrock Edition, is a unique type of slab available through commands or by upgrading from legacy versions. Unlike all other slabs, they are unobtainable in vanilla Survival gameplay.
entities.name: Petrified Oak Slab

entities.blurb: A piglin head is the head of a piglin in the form of a block. It can only be obtained by killing a piglin using a charged creeper's explosion.
entities.name: Piglin Head

entities.blurb: Heads (including skulls) are a group of 7  blocks based on the heads of players and 6 different mobs. All heads can be worn as helmets and serve as special note block instruments.
entities.name: Piglin Wall Head

entities.blurb: A banner is a block that can be crafted in 16 different colors, customized in a loom using dyes and banner patterns, and applied to a shield. In Java Edition, banners can also be used to add markers to maps.
entities.name: Pink Banner

entities.blurb: A bed is a dyeable utility block that allows a player in the Overworld to sleep through the night and change their spawn point to within a few blocks of the bed, as long as it is not broken or obstructed. Villagers sleep in beds at night and require spare beds to produce offspring.
entities.name: Pink Bed

entities.blurb:
A candle is a dyable block that emits light when lit with a flint and steel. Up to four of the same color of candle can be placed in one block space, which affects the amount of light produced.
Dyed candles are the dyed variants of candles that come in all sixteen colors. Once dyed, they cannot be changed into a different color.
entities.name: Pink Candle

entities.blurb:
A cake is a block that can serve as food. It can be eaten by placing and using it, with each use consuming one of its seven slices. The entire cake gives the most hunger points out of every food item, but has low saturation.
A cake with candle is an uneaten cake with any type of candle placed on it, which can be lit with a flint and steel to emit light.
entities.name: Cake with Pink Candle

entities.blurb: Carpets are thin variants of wool that can be dyed in any of the 16 colors.
entities.name: Pink Carpet

entities.blurb: Concrete is a block created when concrete powder touches water. It comes in the sixteen dye colors.
entities.name: Pink Concrete

entities.blurb: Concrete powder is a gravity-affected block that is converted to concrete when touching water. It comes in the sixteen dye colors.
entities.name: Pink Concrete Powder

entities.blurb: Concrete slabs are a craftable slab variant of concrete. They come in 16 colors.
entities.name: Pink Concrete Slab

entities.blurb: Concrete stairs are a craftable stair variant of concrete. They come in 16 colors.
entities.name: Pink Concrete Stairs

entities.blurb: Glazed terracotta is a vibrant solid block that comes in the sixteen regular dye colors, obtained by smelting stained terracotta. Glazed terracotta does not stick to slime blocks or honey blocks, and it cannot be pulled by sticky pistons, but it can be pushed by pistons.
entities.name: Pink Glazed Terracotta

entities.blurb: Pink petals are a decorative block that generates in cherry grove biomes.
entities.name: Pink Petals

entities.blurb: A shulker box is a dyeable block that stores items, and, unlike all other storage blocks, keeps its contents in item form when broken.
entities.name: Pink Shulker Box

entities.blurb: Stained glass is a dyed variant of the glass block.
entities.name: Pink Stained Glass

entities.blurb: A stained glass pane is a dyed version of a glass pane. It is a transparent block that can be used as a more efficient alternative to stained glass blocks.
entities.name: Pink Stained Glass Pane

entities.blurb: Stained terracotta is a dyed variant of terracotta obtained by crafting undyed terracotta with dyes. Some of the variants are found in badlands biomes, and all variants can be smelted into glazed terracotta.
entities.name: Pink Terracotta

entities.blurb: Flowers are plants that occur in a variety of shapes and colors. Many of them can be crafted into various types of dye and/or suspicious stew, and some have unique properties. Bees collect nectar from most flower types, which they use to fill their home nests and hives with honey. Additionally, most flower types can be used to breed bees.
entities.name: Pink Tulip

entities.blurb: A banner is a block that can be crafted in 16 different colors, customized in a loom using dyes and banner patterns, and applied to a shield. In Java Edition, banners can also be used to add markers to maps.
entities.name: Pink Wall Banner

entities.blurb: Wool is a block obtained from sheep that can be dyed in any of the sixteen different colors. It can be used as a crafting material and to block vibrations.
entities.name: Pink Wool

entities.blurb: A wool slab is a craftable slab variant of wool. It can be dyed in all 16 colors.
entities.name: Pink Wool Slab

entities.blurb: Wool stairs are a craftable stair variant of wool. They can be dyed in all 16 colors.
entities.name: Pink Wool Stairs

entities.blurb:
A piston is a block capable of pushing most entities and blocks when given a redstone signal. 
Some blocks cannot be moved, break when pushed or have other interactions with pistons. A piston can move up to twelve blocks at once.
entities.name: Piston

entities.blurb: Pistons and sticky pistons have 2 technical blocks that cannot be obtained. These include the piston head and moving piston blocks.
entities.name: Piston Head

entities.blurb: A pitcher pod is an ancient bulbous seed that has a chance to be dropped by sniffers when they finish digging. It is the seed of pitcher plants.
entities.name: Pitcher Crop

entities.blurb: A pitcher plant is a tall ancient flower that grows from a pitcher pod.
entities.name: Pitcher Plant

entities.blurb: The player head is a block based on the head of a player's skin (Steve by default). Player heads cannot be obtained in Survival.
entities.name: Player Head

entities.blurb: Heads (including skulls) are a group of 7  blocks based on the heads of players and 6 different mobs. All heads can be worn as helmets and serve as special note block instruments.
entities.name: Player Wall Head

entities.blurb: Podzol is a dirt-type block that naturally blankets the surface of the old growth taiga and bamboo jungles, along with their respective variants. Grass blocks and mycelium cannot spread to this block.
entities.name: Podzol

entities.blurb:
Pointed dripstone is a block found in dripstone caves that forms stalactites and stalagmites.
Stalactites (which point downward) grow over time under certain conditions, can serve as falling projectiles, can renewably drip water and lava into cauldrons and convert mud into clay.
Stalagmites (which point upward) deal extra damage to players and mobs that land on them.
entities.name: Pointed Dripstone

entities.blurb: Polished andesite is the polished version of andesite.
entities.name: Polished Andesite

entities.blurb: A polished andesite slab is a decorative slab variant of polished andesite that does not generate naturally and is used for building.
entities.name: Polished Andesite Slab

entities.blurb: Polished andesite stairs are a decorative stairs variant of polished andesite used for building.
entities.name: Polished Andesite Stairs

entities.blurb: Polished basalt is the polished version of basalt and can be found as part of ancient cities and bastion remnants.
entities.name: Polished Basalt

entities.blurb: Polished blackstone is the stone-like polished variation of blackstone.
entities.name: Polished Blackstone
